name: Delamination
desc: The scene turns out to be a coated surface, and the coating is letting go — adhesion fails at the edges first, so a chip cracks a hairline outline around itself, lifts and curls up off its own spot throwing a soft shadow beneath it, then releases and drifts a short way before it is gone, leaving what is behind it clean; aged paint, gold leaf over red bole, lifting photographic emulsion, char with an ember edge, or a conservator's loss map in pure contour.

energy.doc: raking-lamp gain — how hard the lifted chips are lit, how bright their curled edges fire and how deep their shadows sit

scale.doc: chip size — max lifts big slabs of coating instead of fine flakes

speed.doc: how fast the coating fails — a chip's whole life from hairline crack to gone (0.2 still visibly lifts)

density.doc: how much of the surface is failing at once — keep low to stay polite over a scene

veil.doc: how visible the still-adhered coating is — its faint tint and the hairline cracks that predict where the next chip will lift; 0 shows only chips already in flight

hue.doc: hue of the coating (gilt, emulsion and ash keep their own material colour)

x.doc: horizontal drift of the failing region

y.doc: vertical drift of the failing region

style.doc: aesthetic: matte aged paint under a raking lamp / gold leaf flaking off dark red bole / photographic emulsion lifting away milky and silver / charred film with a faint ember edge / a conservator's loss map in pure contour, no fill, no light

seed.doc: deterministic seed for chip shape, placement, phase offset and drift direction

alpha.doc: layer opacity — defaults low so the scene behind stays legible
